sources.title: Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria 1999
sources.catalogue_note: Later amendments have not yet been checked, so no consolidated text is offered here. Use the official source for the current text.
sources.summary: The supreme law of Nigeria: it sets up the federal government, the states and the courts, and guarantees fundamental rights.

sources.title: Central Bank of Nigeria Act 2007
sources.catalogue_note: The official copy is published by the Central Bank of Nigeria. Amendments since 2007 have not yet been checked.
sources.summary: Establishes the Central Bank of Nigeria and sets out its objects, powers and governance.

sources.title: Freedom of Information Act 2011
sources.catalogue_note: The official link leads to the Federal Ministry of Justice's page for the Act.
sources.summary: Gives everyone a right of access to records and information held by public institutions in Nigeria.

sources.title: Investments and Securities Act 2007
sources.catalogue_note: Repealed by section 356 of the Investments and Securities Act 2025, in force from 25 March 2025. Kept for historical reference.
sources.summary: Regulated Nigeria's capital market and the Securities and Exchange Commission until it was replaced.

sources.title: Investments and Securities Act 2025
sources.catalogue_note: The official link is the Act as printed in the Federal Republic of Nigeria Official Gazette (No. 19, Vol. 112, 2 May 2025), published by the Securities and Exchange Commission. In force from 25 March 2025; later amendments have not yet been checked.
sources.summary: Regulates Nigeria's capital market and establishes the Securities and Exchange Commission as its apex regulator, replacing the Investments and Securities Act 2007.
